answer: Each agent must burn an asymmetric anchor of verifiable computation bound to a rotating committee quorum, so identity cost scales with Byzantine-fault-tolerant replication rather than registration. A cipher commits the agent to a threshold-shared secret whose misbehavior triggers slashing across honest replicas, forcing attackers to corrupt a third of stake per identity. An adversary cannot forge cheaply: replicating one sybil costs full quorum collateral, though colluding majorities remain the limit.
